title: A cash-secured put is not 'getting paid to buy a stock you like'
summary: The speaker, a former senior PM at a $14 billion hedge fund, rejects the line that a short put pays you to buy a stock at your price. A short put assigns you when the market chooses, often while it is falling. With a risk-first mindset you buy stocks at your price, not where someone puts you into a trade.

steps.caption: A $100 stock. Sell a 30-day put at $95, the 'price you want to pay'.
If the stock stays above $95, you keep a small premium.
Below the breakeven the trade loses money.
In a crash you are assigned on the way down. You catch a falling knife.
You are short volatility. You do not choose the entry; the market does.

takeaways: A short put is a short volatility trade, not a limit order with a bonus.
Assignment usually happens when the market is falling hard.
Buy stocks at your own entry point.
